On 11 March 1990 the newly elected parliament of Lithuania declared the independence of the state restored. It was the first Soviet republic to break away.

The Sąjūdis movement, born in 1988, had won the elections. Its leader Vytautas Landsbergis became head of state. Moscow answered with an economic blockade, and in January 1991 Soviet troops stormed the Vilnius television tower, killing fourteen unarmed civilians. Crowds kept guard around parliament.

Iceland was the first state to recognise Lithuania, in February 1991. After the failed coup in Moscow that August, the world followed, and the Soviet Union itself broke up by the end of the year. The act restored the state of 1918. See Lithuania.
sum: On 11 March 1990 the newly elected parliament of Lithuania declared the independence of the state restored. It was the first Soviet republic to break away.
